# From one discharge to a population

## The question turns around

Sessions 01--05 went deeper into one discharge. Session 06 asks:

> Where in operational and MHD-stability space do the reconstructed VEST states lie ---
> and which statements about limits does the evidence support?

$$\text{history} \rightarrow \text{summary contracts} \rightarrow \text{population}
\rightarrow \text{reference boundaries} \rightarrow \text{stability join} \rightarrow \text{classification}$$

::: {.notes}
[2 min]

NARRATE:
Everything runs offline from two repository-only sample collections,
vest_operational_history and vest_tier_a, read with vaft.data.data_path. Their
manifests carry the hashes the notebook checks before any number is shown.

TRANSITION:
Start with the longest record: the shot history.
:::

## Four things drawn on one plane

| term | evidence it needs |
| --- | --- |
| observed envelope | the population itself |
| accessible operating space | engineering limits, scans |
| empirical / theoretical boundary | source, domain, quantity definitions |
| solver classification | the solver, its inputs, its numerical QA |

An empty region is not by itself an operating limit.

::: {.notes}
[3 min]

NARRATE:
Keep the four apart for the whole session. Most mistakes in operational-space
plots are one of these being read as another.
:::

# Operational history and summary contracts

## The archived history is history, not a preset

- 2257 shots, 38000--45767; 1932 with max $I_p \geq 2$ kA; 1382 with a legacy EFIT ODS
- no pulse date, no `shot_class`, no onset source: shot number $\neq$ calendar time
- the 32 Tier A shots occupy two narrow bands of shot numbers

::: {.notes}
[4 min]

NARRATE:
Compare the archived columns with the shot_overview contract column by column.
The 2 kA cut borrows the pickup threshold of shot_class; it is not a
classification.
:::

## A preset is a definition

| preset | reads | grain / key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `shot_overview` | spectrometer_uv, magnetics, tf, barometry, dataset_description | shot |
| `equilibrium_global` | equilibrium, magnetics, tf | `(shot, eq_index, time_s)` |
| `core_profiles` | equilibrium, core_profiles, magnetics, tf | `(shot, cp_index, time_s)` |

`summary(odss=...)` runs the same extractor offline; `attrs["skipped"]` names the
shots it could not build (48224: no plasma current, `PlasmaTimingError`).

::: {.notes}
[4 min]

NARRATE:
shot_overview takes its window from plasma_timing (H-alpha first, I_p as a
cross-check) and classifies Plasma / BD failure / Vacuum. Always print skipped.

TRANSITION:
Offline extraction is one of three access paths.
:::

## Lazy, eager, offline

- `open(shot, paths=...)`: read-only, lazy, inside a `with` block; few leaves of many shots
- `load(shot)`: eager, materialised; one shot to modify or run codes on
- `summary(shot_range=...)`: lazy per shot, only the preset's IDS
- `summary(odss=...)`: no database at all

Database calls run only in lab mode, read-only.

::: {.notes}
[2 min]

NARRATE:
The same shot number in two sources is two reconstructions; every population
row therefore carries its lineage.
:::

# The Tier A population

## Grain, joins and names

- 150 states from 32 shots: 133 magnetics + 17 electron-kinetic, good or admissible
- five tables, five grains: shot, state, state $\times n$, state $\times n \times$ solver $\times$ surface
- join on `(shot, round(t * 1e6), lineage)`, `validate="one_to_one"`: 150 / 0 / 0
- two "internal inductance" columns differ by 1.00--1.51$\times$: a name is not a definition

::: {.notes}
[4 min]

NARRATE:
The atlas spells the lineages magnetics-only and electron-kinetic; map them
explicitly and refuse unknown labels. Joining a per-state table to atlas_n
without reducing it first multiplies every state by six.
:::

## Reconstructed, selected, sparse

- $q_{95}$, $l_i$, $\beta_p$, $W_\mathrm{MHD}$ are EFIT outputs: joint inference, not two measured axes
- `efit_quality` (trustworthy equilibrium) $\neq$ `selected` (usable power balance)
- Thomson density on 64/133 states; scalings only there
- H (selected, median): ITER89P 0.75, H98y2 0.72, NSTX2006L 0.24

::: {.notes}
[3 min]

NARRATE:
One state per shot versus all slices changes every distribution; say which
population a statistic describes.
:::

# Operating space

## Field conventions and quantity identities

- $I_N$, $q^*$, Hugill: vacuum $B_T$ at $R_\mathrm{geo}$; stored $\beta_N$: $B_T$ at $R_0 = 0.4$ m
- $\beta_N(R_\mathrm{geo}) = \beta_N(R_0)\,R_\mathrm{geo}/R_0$, factor 0.73--1.14
- $q_{95} \neq q_\psi \neq q(a) \neq q^*$; DCON `qlim` sits at $\psi_N = 0.994$
- Wesson and Cheng panels: reference only; Strait $4\,l_i(1)$ never on an $l_i(3)$ axis

::: {.notes}
[4 min]

NARRATE:
vaft.plot.operational_space draws a boundary only where the column's quantity
and unit match the axis, and reports what it omitted.
:::

## Reading the planes

- $q^* I_N = 5\kappa/A$ (4.4--6.7): the $q^*$--$I_N$ plane is mostly shape
- the kink boundary is OUTSIDE its calibration for a spherical tokamak; the rest are UNASSESSED
- the Troyon plane re-expresses $\beta_N$; it adds no independent measurement
- spherical-tokamak Hugill (Sykes 2000) is the native density plane for VEST

::: {.notes}
[4 min]

NARRATE:
Read the applicability line before the boundary. Unless a boundary is
SUPPORTED, it is a reference, not a VEST limit.
:::

# Stability

## Layers stay separate

1. raw: $W_t$ per $n$ and edge; $\Delta'$ per surface
2. QA: sign at two resolutions (`sign_class`, `two_resolution_consistent`)
3. criterion: $W_t<0$; $\Delta'>0$; $D_I>0$; $D_R>0$; $C_A<0$
4. interpretation: not produced --- $\Delta'>0$ is a classical drive, not a tearing verdict

Not assessed is never stable.

::: {.notes}
[3 min]

NARRATE:
A state can be ideal-stable at every n, carry a QA-supported Delta-prime and be
Mercier-stable at once. Keep all three flags.
:::

## What the atlas says

- DCON full edge: 129 stable / 13 unstable / 8 unresolved; truncated edge: 146 / 3 / 1
- $\Delta'>0$ raw on most states, QA-supported on 9 (RDCON) and 38 (STRIDE); a failed run is not assessed, never a drive
- $D_R>0$ on 124, $D_I>0$ on 1, $C_A<0$ on 12
- magnitudes are not growth rates; no "marginal" band without a derived threshold

::: {.notes}
[5 min]

NARRATE:
The edge treatment decides most ideal verdicts; report both. The gap between
raw and QA-supported drive is a statement about numerics, not tearing. The
legacy pipeline-3 sheets collapsed all of this into one label with fixed
magnitude cut-offs, which is why they are not plotted.
:::

## Takeaways

- presets are definitions; print `skipped`
- archived tables are history; shot number $\neq$ time
- lazy for many shots, eager for one, `odss=` offline
- envelope $\neq$ limit; boundaries only on their own quantity, with applicability
- join at the native grain and print the report
- ideal, resistive, local and QA are separate layers

::: {.notes}
[2 min]

NARRATE:
End of the course. Session 01 opened one discharge; session 06 put it among the
others. Regression, similarity, events and learning are optional extensions on
top of a population defined this carefully.
:::
